summary: First-run full-stack test of ZYRA. Backend pytest: 16/16 passing (leads CRUD, validation, admin auth, token gating, patch persistence, brute-force lockout eventually triggers). Frontend Playwright: all 16 routes render (200), plus /search, /product/p1, /pairs/pair-midnight-formal, /admin and 404 page all work. PAIR colour/size on home updates availability; occasion-first buttons swap results; all 4 lead forms (waitlist, merchant, investor, contact) validate and submit successfully with success panels; search returns 1 result for 'sherwani' and shows the empty state for nonsense queries; product colour/size updates availability and add-to-bag shows the launch toast; admin login rejects wrong creds, accepts admin@zyra.app / ZyraAdmin2026, shows admin-stats and admin-leads, PATCH status persists after reload, and logout returns to login form; mobile 390px opens the drawer (9 links) and the sticky CTA is visible.

minor.issue: Brute-force lockout counter keys off request.client.host (ingress/proxy IP). Because k8s ingress load-balances across replicas, the source IP seen by FastAPI can differ per request, so the count of failed attempts is not per-user-reliable. 429 does trigger, but only after 6-15 attempts instead of exactly 5. Fix: honour X-Forwarded-For (starlette request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for').split(',')[0]) when building the identifier.

CORSMiddleware is configured with allow_credentials=True AND allow_origins can be '*' from env (current .env has CORS_ORIGINS='*'). Browsers reject credentialed requests when Access-Control-Allow-Origin is '*'. The current frontend uses Bearer tokens in localStorage so it works today, but if cookie-based auth is used cross-origin it will fail silently. Set CORS_ORIGINS to explicit origins.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py: get_current_admin does ObjectId(payload['sub']) without try/except; a malformed sub in a hand-crafted JWT would raise a 500 instead of 401. Wrap in try/except and raise 401.
server.py: rate_limit is per-process in-memory (_hits dict); useless behind multiple workers/replicas. Same class of issue as the lockout: use a shared store (Mongo/Redis) or accept as best-effort.
server.py: check_lockout / register_failure keyed on request.client.host — see backend minor issue above.

server.py: on startup, if admin email exists but password matches, role isn't corrected; if it doesn't match, role is force-updated to admin. Fine, but consider always upserting role='admin' for the seed admin.
seed_data_creation: Created ~1 waitlist + 1 merchant + 1 investor + 1 contact lead via UI, plus 4 leads (one per type) via pytest with TEST_ prefixed names/emails. One lead status was updated to 'reviewed' via the admin dashboard.
